title: Robinson R44 Raven I / II

sources.title: X-Plane R22 Beta II Pilot Operating Manual (Laminar Research)
JoyPro function tables MSFS2020/2024 and X-Plane 11/12 (DB/Functions)

intro: The Robinson R44 is a small four-seat piston helicopter. Its cockpit has a single T-bar cyclic between the front seats, a collective lever with a twist-grip throttle at the left of each front seat and an instrument console in the middle.

areas.name: Instrument console
areas.text: The dashboard in the middle of the cockpit with the dials for speed, height, horizon, climb rate and engine and rotor speed, plus the warning lights.

panels.name: Instrument console
panels.text: This console holds the flight dials and the engine gauges, together with the warning and annunciator lights that tell the pilot when something is wrong.
panels.context: The pilot watches the rotor and engine gauges closely, because the rotor must turn at the right speed for the helicopter to fly.

controls.name: Vertical speed indicator
controls.text: This dial shows how fast the helicopter climbs or sinks.
controls.context: The pilot uses it to hold a steady climb or descent.

controls.name: Attitude indicator
controls.text: This dial shows the artificial horizon: whether the nose is up or down and whether the helicopter leans to a side.
controls.context: The pilot uses it when the real horizon cannot be seen.

controls.name: Airspeed indicator
controls.text: This dial shows how fast the helicopter flies through the air.
controls.context: The pilot checks the speed in every phase of the flight.

controls.name: Engine and rotor tachometer
controls.text: This dial has two needles. One shows how fast the engine turns and the other how fast the main rotor turns, in revolutions per minute (RPM). They normally stay together.
controls.context: The pilot keeps the needles in the green range. If the rotor turns too slowly, the helicopter cannot fly.

controls.name: Manifold pressure indicator
controls.text: This dial shows the manifold pressure, how hard air is pushed into the piston engine. It tells the pilot how much power the engine is giving.
controls.context: The pilot watches it so that the power does not go above the limit.

controls.name: Altimeter
controls.text: This dial shows the height above sea level.
controls.context: The pilot sets the local air pressure on it so the height reads right.

controls.name: Annunciator lights
controls.text: These lights tell about the clutch, the main rotor gearbox (MR temp and chip), low fuel, low rotor rpm and carbon monoxide.
controls.context: A lit light is a call to action. For example, low rpm means the pilot must lower the collective at once.

controls.name: Warning lights
controls.text: These lights show a failed alternator (ALT), low oil pressure (OIL) and that the governor is off (GOV OFF).
controls.context: The pilot reads the light and follows the checklist for it.

areas.name: Overhead: rotor brake
areas.text: The ceiling area above the pilot, with the rotor brake.

panels.name: Main rotor brake
panels.text: The main rotor is the big spinning wing on top. After the engine has stopped, the rotor brake stops it faster by pressing on its drive.
panels.context: The pilot uses it at the end of the flight, after the engine shut down. It stays off in flight.

controls.name: Main rotor brake
controls.text: Pulling this handle presses a brake onto the rotor drive so that the rotor stops turning sooner after the engine is off.
controls.context: The pilot uses it only after shutdown on the ground and never in flight.

areas.name: Lower console
areas.text: The console between and below the seats with the starter key, the electric switches, the engine gauges and the engine controls.

panels.name: Switch panel and lower console
panels.text: This area holds the starter key, the electrical switches, the carburettor temperature gauge, the engine gauges, and the mixture, carburettor heat and fuel valve controls.
panels.context: The pilot uses it for the start-up and shutdown, and the carburettor heat when ice might form.

controls.name: Starter key

positions.name: OFF
positions.text: Both magnetos are off and the engine is stopped.

positions.name: R
positions.text: Only the right magneto works; used for a check.

positions.name: L
positions.text: Only the left magneto works; used for a check.

positions.name: BOTH
positions.text: Both magnetos work. This is the normal running position.

positions.name: START
positions.text: The starter turns the engine; the key springs back to BOTH.

controls.text: This key switch works the magnetos, the two spark makers of the piston engine, and the starter. Turning it to START spins the engine.
controls.context: After the engine runs, the pilot leaves the key on BOTH, and it springs back from START.

controls.name: Electrical panel
controls.text: These switches connect the battery and the alternator to the electric system, run the clutch and turn on the lights.
controls.context: The pilot switches the battery on first. The clutch connects the engine to the rotor after the start.

controls.name: Carburettor temperature gauge
controls.text: This gauge shows the temperature of the air in the carburettor, the part that mixes fuel and air. A cold reading means ice could form.
controls.context: Ice in the carburettor can stop the engine, so the pilot watches this gauge and uses carburettor heat if needed.

controls.name: Engine instrument cluster
controls.text: This group of small dials shows the oil pressure and temperature, the fuel amount, the cylinder head temperature (CHT) and the ammeter, which shows the electric current.
controls.context: The pilot checks them during the start and during the flight to see that the engine is healthy.

controls.name: Cyclic friction control
controls.text: This knob sets how stiff the cyclic stick feels. Turning it makes the stick harder to move, so it stays where the pilot puts it.
controls.context: Friction can help the pilot hold the stick steady, but too much makes it hard to fly.

controls.name: Mixture control
controls.text: This control sets the fuel-to-air mixture of the engine, from rich to idle cut-off. Pulling it all the way stops the engine.
controls.context: The pilot sets it rich for the start and the flight, and pulls it to cut-off to stop the engine.

controls.name: Carburettor heat control
controls.text: Pulling this control warms the air going into the carburettor to melt ice.
controls.context: The pilot uses it when the gauge shows that ice could form. It costs a little engine power.

controls.name: Fuel shutoff valve
controls.text: This control opens or closes the fuel line from the tanks to the engine.
controls.context: It stays on in normal flight. The pilot closes it in an emergency or after the flight.

areas.name: Cyclic, collective and pedals
areas.text: The controls for the pilot's hands and feet: the T-bar cyclic, the collective with its throttle and the pedals.

panels.name: T-bar cyclic
panels.text: The cyclic is a column in the middle between the front seats with a T-shaped bar on top. The pilot holds it with the right hand. A push-to-talk trigger sits on the bar.
panels.context: The pilot steers the helicopter's direction in the air with it.

controls.name: T-bar cyclic
controls.text: Moving the cyclic forward tilts the rotor so the helicopter moves forward. Moving it back goes backwards and moving it sideways goes sideways.
controls.context: It does not change the height. It changes the direction the helicopter moves in.

controls.name: Push-to-talk
controls.text: Pressing this trigger on the cyclic bar makes the radio send while it is held.
controls.context: The pilot uses it to talk to the controller.

panels.name: Collective with throttle
panels.text: The collective is the lever at the left of the pilot's seat. The left hand holds it. The twist grip on its end is the engine throttle.
panels.context: The collective sets the lift, and the twist grip sets the engine power.

controls.name: Collective
controls.text: Pulling this lever up makes the rotor blades bite the air harder, so the helicopter climbs. Lowering it makes the helicopter sink.
controls.context: The pilot lifts the lever to lift off and lowers it to land.

controls.name: Twist-grip throttle
controls.text: Twisting the grip on the end of the collective changes the engine power. It is linked to the collective, and the governor helps hold the rotor speed.
controls.context: The pilot adjusts it so the rotor speed stays in the green range.

controls.name: Governor switch

positions.name: on
positions.text: The governor keeps the rotor speed by itself.

positions.name: off
positions.text: The governor is off and the pilot works the throttle by hand.

controls.text: This switch at the end of the collective turns the governor on or off. The governor is a helper that holds the rotor speed by moving the throttle by itself.
controls.context: The governor is on in normal flight. If it is off, the pilot must hold the rotor speed with the throttle by hand.

controls.name: Landing lights switch
controls.text: This switch on the collective turns the landing light on or off.
controls.context: The pilot uses the landing light to see the ground in the dark.

panels.name: Anti-torque pedals
panels.text: The two pedals at the pilot's feet on the floor of the cockpit.
panels.context: The pilot turns the helicopter's nose left and right with them.

controls.name: Anti-torque pedals
controls.text: Pushing a pedal changes the pitch of the tail rotor blades. The tail rotor is the small rotor at the back, and the pedals turn the nose left or right.
controls.context: The pilot uses them to keep the helicopter pointed straight and to turn it while hovering.
